newsitem.title: UK: Currency rules on UK grain cash/futures markets.
newsitem.headline: Currency rules on UK grain cash/futures markets.

text.p: Volatile currencies were again the main feature of the UK grain markets on Thursday.
"The market is more about currency than grain at the moment," said one trader.
Easier sterling against the mark pushed wheat futures up by as much as 1.15 stg a tonne while barley was up to 0.57 stg higher.
However, firm futures kept the cash markets quiet.
"Only the futures boys are trading, no one else wants to know," said a trader.
The result of the European Union (EU) weekly grain tender came too late to affect the futures market but traders said it was friendly.
The EU granted 429,300 tonnes of free market soft wheat at a 19.45 Ecus rebate and 211,000 tonnes of free market barley at a 30.99 Ecus rebate.
Traders said the market had been looking for around 500,000 tonnes of wheat and this was near enough.
"If sterling stays around its current level against the mark the market will go up again on Friday," said one trader.
"The market won't go screaming up, but it's friendly," said another.
At the close wheat futures were 1.15 to 0.50 stg up with most traded May one stg above Wednesday's close with a last trade of 98.60 stg after trading 276 lots.
Barley finished 0.75 to 0.65 stg up with most traded Jan 0.75 stg up on 100 lots.
Wheat traded a total of 566 lots and barley 135 lots.
Amsterdam milling wheat futures were neglected.
Cash trade was at a virtual standstill.
